patterns.summary: Nginx cannot connect to upstream backend application server
patterns.root_cause: The backend application server is not running, not listening on the configured port, or unreachable due to network/firewall issues. Nginx proxy_pass is trying to forward requests but the upstream is down.
patterns.impact: All requests to this service return 502 errors. Users cannot access the application. API endpoints are unavailable.

patterns.summary: Upstream server took too long to respond
patterns.root_cause: Backend application is overloaded, processing requests slowly, or has hanging processes. Nginx timeout settings are too aggressive for the workload.
patterns.impact: Slow or failed requests. Degraded user experience with timeouts.

patterns.summary: Kubernetes pod is repeatedly crashing and restarting
patterns.root_cause: Container application exits immediately after starting due to: application errors, missing dependencies, misconfigured environment variables, failed health checks, or insufficient resources (OOMKilled).
patterns.impact: Service unavailable. Pod cannot serve traffic. Deployment is failing.

patterns.summary: Kubernetes cannot pull container image from registry
patterns.root_cause: Image doesn't exist, wrong image name/tag, registry authentication failed, or network connectivity issues to container registry.
patterns.impact: Pod stuck in ImagePullBackOff. Cannot deploy new containers. Service deployment blocked.

patterns.summary: Pod cannot be scheduled to any node
patterns.root_cause: Insufficient cluster resources (CPU/memory), node selector mismatch, taints/tolerations issues, or persistent volume claim problems.
patterns.impact: Pod cannot start. Service capacity reduced or unavailable.

patterns.summary: Application cannot connect to PostgreSQL database
patterns.root_cause: PostgreSQL service not running, not listening on expected address/port, pg_hba.conf authentication misconfigured, or firewall blocking port 5432.
patterns.impact: Database-dependent features fail. Application errors. Data cannot be read/written.

patterns.summary: Database transactions are deadlocked
patterns.root_cause: Multiple transactions trying to acquire locks in conflicting order. Common with concurrent updates to same records without proper transaction isolation.
patterns.impact: Transaction failures. Data inconsistency risk. Application errors on write operations.

patterns.summary: Filesystem has reached capacity
patterns.root_cause: Disk filled by log accumulation, large temporary files, database growth, or insufficient disk allocation. Possible inode exhaustion.
patterns.impact: Cannot write new files. Application crashes. Database writes fail. System instability.

patterns.summary: Process killed due to memory exhaustion
patterns.root_cause: Application exceeded memory limits. Possible memory leak, processing large datasets, or insufficient memory allocation for workload.
patterns.impact: Service crash. Data processing failure. User requests fail.

patterns.summary: JVM ran out of heap memory
patterns.root_cause: Insufficient heap size (-Xmx), memory leak in application code, or processing datasets larger than allocated heap.
patterns.impact: Application crash. Request failures. Service unavailable.

patterns.summary: Container networking problem
patterns.root_cause: Docker network misconfiguration, containers in different networks, DNS resolution failure, or port mapping issues.
patterns.impact: Containers cannot communicate. Service mesh broken. Microservices disconnected.

patterns.summary: SSL/TLS certificate has expired
patterns.root_cause: Certificate validity period ended. Certificate not renewed before expiration date.
patterns.impact: HTTPS connections fail. Browser warnings. API clients reject connections. Service inaccessible via HTTPS.

patterns.summary: Cannot connect to Redis server
patterns.root_cause: Redis service down, network latency, firewall blocking port 6379, or Redis configured for different bind address.
patterns.impact: Caching layer unavailable. Application slowdown. Session storage failures.

patterns.summary: Elasticsearch cluster in RED health state
patterns.root_cause: Unassigned shards, node failures, disk space issues on nodes, or split-brain scenario.
patterns.impact: Data loss risk. Search functionality degraded. Index operations may fail.

patterns.summary: Kafka consumer falling behind
patterns.root_cause: Consumer processing too slow, consumer group rebalancing issues, or insufficient consumer instances for partition count.
patterns.impact: Event processing delays. Real-time features lag. Potential message loss if retention exceeded.

patterns.summary: Cannot resolve domain name to IP
patterns.root_cause: DNS server unreachable, incorrect DNS configuration, domain doesn't exist, or network connectivity issues.
patterns.impact: Cannot reach external services. API calls fail. Service dependencies unavailable.

patterns.summary: Insufficient file system permissions
patterns.root_cause: Process running with insufficient privileges, incorrect file ownership, or restrictive file permissions (chmod).
patterns.impact: Cannot read/write files. Application startup failures. Configuration cannot be loaded.

patterns.summary: Cannot bind to port - already occupied
patterns.root_cause: Another process is already listening on the port. Previous process not cleanly shut down, or port conflict in configuration.
patterns.impact: Service cannot start. Port binding fails. Application initialization blocked.

patterns.summary: Connection attempt timed out
patterns.root_cause: Target service not responding, network latency, firewall dropping packets, or routing issues.
patterns.impact: External API calls fail. Microservice communication broken. Integration failures.

patterns.summary: NPM cannot reach package registry
patterns.root_cause: Network connectivity issues, firewall blocking npm registry, proxy misconfiguration, or npm registry downtime.
patterns.impact: Cannot install dependencies. Build process fails. CI/CD pipeline blocked.
